mcqs.learning_point: Understand the importance of checking product information
mcqs.question: Riya wants to buy a packaged cereal. Which of the following actions best demonstrates the importance of checking product information provided by certification marks?

options.A: She chooses the cereal only because it is the cheapest option
options.B: She looks for an ISI or Agmark label and reads the details printed on it
options.C: She buys the brand she likes without looking at any label
options.D: She selects the biggest pack regardless of any label

mcqs.answer: She looks for an ISI or Agmark label and reads the details printed on it
mcqs.explanation: Checking the certification label (such as ISI or Agmark) and reading the information ensures the product meets recognised safety and quality standards. The other options ignore product information and may lead to unsafe or substandard purchases.

mcqs.question: A consumer sees a washing machine with a 'Standardisation Mark' indicating it meets certain safety criteria. Which statement best describes what this mark signifies?

options.A: The washing machine is the cheapest model available
options.B: The washing machine complies with nationally set safety and quality standards
options.C: The washing machine is manufactured locally
options.D: The washing machine comes with a five‑year warranty

mcqs.answer: The washing machine complies with nationally set safety and quality standards
mcqs.explanation: Standardisation marks show that the product has been tested and conforms to the standards prescribed by a national body (e.g., BIS). Price, origin, or warranty are not indicated by the mark.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the ISI mark is correct?

options.A: It guarantees the product is the cheapest in the market
options.B: It indicates the product meets Indian Standards set by the Bureau of Indian Standards
options.C: It is applied only to electronic items
options.D: It is a marketing slogan with no regulatory backing

mcqs.answer: It indicates the product meets Indian Standards set by the Bureau of Indian Standards
mcqs.explanation: The ISI mark is a certification by the Bureau of Indian Standards confirming that the product conforms to the relevant Indian Standard. It does not guarantee price, is not limited to electronics, and has legal significance.

mcqs.question: A farmer wants to sell his apples under the Agmark label. Which condition must be satisfied for the Agmark certification?

options.A: The apples must be grown in any country
options.B: The apples must meet the quality standards specified for that commodity by the Agricultural Marketing Department
options.C: The apples must be packaged in plastic containers
options.D: The farmer must pay a fixed fee irrespective of the quality of the apples

mcqs.answer: The apples must meet the quality standards specified for that commodity by the Agricultural Marketing Department
mcqs.explanation: Agmark certification is granted only when the agricultural produce complies with the prescribed quality parameters for that specific commodity. Origin, packaging material, or fee alone do not qualify a product for Agmark.

mcqs.question: How does the Hallmark certification for gold jewellery differ from the ISI mark used for industrial products?

options.A: Hallmark assesses purity of gold, while ISI assesses compliance with safety and quality standards for various products
options.B: Hallmark is a global standard, whereas ISI is only for food items
options.C: Both marks certify the same aspects for all kinds of products
options.D: Hallmark is optional, while ISI is mandatory for every good sold in India

mcqs.answer: Hallmark assesses purity of gold, while ISI assesses compliance with safety and quality standards for various products
mcqs.explanation: Hallmark specifically verifies the gold purity (e.g., 22‑carat) in jewellery. ISI, on the other hand, is a broader certification that confirms that a product meets the Indian Standards for safety, quality, and performance across many categories. The other options misrepresent the scope and mandatory nature of the marks.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the importance of checking product information
mcqs.question: In the context of consumer rights, why is it crucial for a buyer to examine the information on a product’s certification mark before purchase?

options.A: It helps the buyer compare prices only
options.B: It provides assurance that the product conforms to safety and quality standards, reducing health risks
options.C: It guarantees the product will never break or malfunction
options.D: It ensures the product is the most fashionable item available

mcqs.answer: It provides assurance that the product conforms to safety and quality standards, reducing health risks
mcqs.explanation: Certification marks convey that an independent agency has verified the product against established standards, giving consumers confidence about safety and quality. Price comparison, durability guarantees, or fashion relevance are not functions of certification marks.

mcqs.question: What is the primary purpose of standardisation marks on consumer products?

options.A: To indicate the product is on sale
options.B: To show the product meets established national standards for quality and safety

mcqs.answer: To show the product meets established national standards for quality and safety
mcqs.explanation: Standardisation marks signal that the product has been tested and conforms to the national standards set for its category, ensuring a baseline of quality and safety. They do not convey pricing, branding, or weight information.

mcqs.question: Which symbol on a product indicates that it has been certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards?
mcqs.explanation: The ISI mark, consisting of the letters 'ISI' within a circle, is the recognizable logo used by the Bureau of Indian Standards to denote that a product complies with the relevant Indian Standard. The other symbols represent unrelated concepts.
